name: William Shakespeare
note:
THERE IS NO MANUSCRIPT. Not one authorial holograph of any Shakespeare play survives. Everything on this shelf descends from printed books, and the printed books disagree.

For roughly twenty plays — The Tempest, Macbeth, Twelfth Night among them — the 1623 Folio is the earliest text of any kind. For others there are competing quarto printings, and the disagreements are not trivial: Hamlet has three early witnesses that differ substantially, and the two texts of King Lear differ far enough that many editors now print them as two plays rather than reconcile them.

So every modern reading edition is an EDITOR'S CONSTRUCTION, assembled by choosing among witnesses. That is honest scholarship and it is not the same thing as a source. This shelf therefore holds both poles: forty-four works split out of the modern Complete Works for reading, and the First Folio entire as the evidence they were constructed from.

THE RULE FOR THIS ROOM: read from the individual works; check contested passages against the Folio.

ONE THING WORTH SEEING. The Folio opens with its own catalogue of the plays it contains, grouped as Comedies, Histories and Tragedies — the grouping used here. Troilus and Cressida does not appear in that list, and is printed in the book anyway. The first collected Shakespeare disagrees with itself about what it is.

FLAGGED, NOT SOLVED. The Two Noble Kinsmen is a collaboration with John Fletcher. The Passionate Pilgrim is a 1599 miscellany published under his name whose contents are largely by other people. Both are here, both are marked, and whether they belong on a separate shelf is undecided.

works.title: The First Folio, 1623
works.source: *Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies* — the First Folio, 1623 · Project Gutenberg #2270 · public domain
works.note: THE WITNESS, NOT THE READING TEXT. Original spelling and punctuation, printed seven years after his death by men who had acted with him. For roughly twenty plays this is the earliest text of any kind. Everything else on this shelf descends from it or from quartos that disagree with it. It exceeds GitHub's display limit and will not render in the browser — it downloads correctly.

works.title: The Sonnets
works.source: William Shakespeare, *The Complete Works* · Project Gutenberg #100 · public domain
works.note: One hundred and fifty-four sonnets, published in 1609 in an order nobody can prove is his. The first hundred and twenty-six address a young man, the rest a woman. Four centuries of readers have tried to make them a story; they resist it.
